trial_court: II Additional Judicial Magistrate of I Class, Tanuku, M.C.No.46 of 2011
case_name: Kadali Durga Rao W G Dt vs Kadali Surya Kumari Wg Dt Anr Rep Pp on 20 January 2021
facts_of_case: Wife filed M.C.No.46 of 2011 seeking maintenance under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. Husband denied paternity of child born in 2010 and sought DNA test to determine paternity.

legal_principles.principle: Conclusive proof of legitimacy is established by the birth of a child during the continuance of a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: Section 112 of the Evidence Act says where during the continuance of valid marriage if a child is born that is a conclusive proof about the legitimacy.

legal_principles.principle: Medical tests cannot be conclusive of paternity.
legal_principles.held: Moreover it is settled law that medical test cannot be conclusive of paternity.

legal_principles.principle: Blood tests can show positively that a given man could or could not be the father, but cannot show positively that any man is the father.
legal_principles.held: Rayden on Divorce, (1983) Vol. 1) p. 1054 has this to say: 'Medical Science is able to analyse the blood of individuals into definite groups: and by examining the blood of a given man and a child to determine whether the man could or could not be the father.'

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
